name: Regensburg Cathedral
_about: REGENSBURG CATHEDRAL (Dom St. Peter) from the same components as Notre-Dame (the `gothic` generator): the `basilica` nave of five bays, 31.85 m to the vault, rib-vaulted on compound piers, flyers down the flanks; a transept that does not project; and no ambulatory but THREE STAGGERED CHOIRS, the main one a bay further east, nearly all glass between deep buttresses, each closed in a polygon; the west front between two towers, the great traceried window over the main portal and before it the TRIANGULAR PORCH on its one pillar under free-standing gables (`triangle-porch`); the towers' open octagons and openwork spires to 105 m; the copper Dachreiter over the crossing; and west of the north transept front the Romanesque Eselsturm. Pale limestone patched with greensand under red-brown tiled roofs.

params._naveW: the nave's and the aisles' clear widths, between the walls' faces
params._arcadeH: the heights the furnishing is laid out to (the organ, the gallery)
params._towerBays: the aisles' last bays at the west end, which the towers stand over: they have no aisle vault or roof of their own
params._towerD: a tower's depth: over the aisle bays it stands on and the west front's 3m -- its back is the next bay's transverse arch
params._crossA: the first of the two bays the crossing spans, from the west (the crossing square: two bays by the nave's width)
params._flyerStages: Notre-Dame's flyers clear both aisles in one leap (rebuilt so in the 1220s); Cologne's in two, from intermediate piers
params._clerSpring: the high vault springs this far over the clerestory sill: Notre-Dame's tall clerestory

church._about: nave, crossing, transept, apse and ambulatory as one vaulted skeleton: piers, arches, rib vaults, buttresses, flyers, roofs

west front._about: the west front between the towers, in three tiers: the central portal; the great rose; the open gallery

towers._about: the two towers, from the ground: a portal in the front, a window, a blind stage, then the belfry's lancet pairs; the back an arch across the aisle

tower stairs._about: the stair up each tower (`tower-stair`): the spiral turret against the outer flank, from the aisle to the terrace on top, which is the floor round its head

front courses._about: the string courses across the whole front

west gable._about: the gable over the great window, between the towers

tower octagons._about: the open octagon on each tower, a tall traceried lancet in every face (`gothic-octagon-stage`)

tower spire feet._about: the gables and pinnacles round each spire's foot (`gothic-spire`)

tower pinnacles._about: a pinnacle on every corner of the towers' heads, where the octagon stage begins

west gallery._about: the organ loft: a gallery across the nave's west bay, the doors passing under it

seating._about: the nave's seating between the arcades, from under the gallery up to the crossing, on a middle aisle

altar._about: the high altar just east of the crossing

organ._about: the great organ on the west gallery, its pipes facing east down the nave

central tympanum._about: the tympanum filling the arch's head, carved in the real one, over its lintel

central archivolt 1._about: a ring of the arch's mouldings

central archivolt 3._about: a ring of the arch's mouldings

north archivolt 2._about: a ring of the arch's mouldings

north archivolt 3._about: a ring of the arch's mouldings

south tympanum._about: the tympanum filling the arch's head, carved in the real one, over its lintel

south archivolt 1._about: a ring of the arch's mouldings

south archivolt 2._about: a ring of the arch's mouldings

south archivolt 3._about: a ring of the arch's mouldings

porch._about: the TRIANGULAR PORCH (Dreieckportal, c. 1410) before the main portal: its tip on one pillar, open in two arches under free-standing gables (`triangle-porch`)

eselsturm._about: the ESELSTURM, the Romanesque tower left from the old cathedral, west of the north transept front: small round-headed openings, paired at the top

dachreiter._about: the Dachreiter over the crossing: a small open lantern and its spire, copper (`domed-tower`)
